kicker: VALUE DYNAMICS  ·  AN ARITHMETIC BORROWED FROM BREEDERS
sub: A judging loop has a population, a selection step, and inheritance. Breeders have equations for that.
narration: Animal and plant breeders have known for a century how to say what a population will look like after selection. Measure how much the trait varies among the individuals you have. Measure how strongly your choice of parents favors it. The change in the next generation follows from those two numbers, before that generation exists.

headline: Response equals heritability times the selection differential
sub: the difference you select for, times the fraction the offspring keep
narration: The selection differential is the mean trait of the parents you breed from minus the mean of the population they came from. Heritability is the fraction of that difference the offspring keep, and it has to be fitted from data. George Price generalized the accounting to any population that varies, selects, and inherits.

caption: The same three ingredients, inside a training loop
narration: Now take a language model that writes candidate answers, has a judge keep the ones it prefers, and is fine-tuned on those. A population that varies. A step that keeps some and discards others. Inheritance, because the kept answers become the training data. Post-training already runs loops shaped like this, with models writing and filtering much of their successors' training data.

headline: Value drift has a name; the trajectories have not been measured
sub: alignment faking · model collapse · attractor states in model-to-model conversation
narration: Alignment research has named the worry. Whether a model defends its values under training, how recursive training degrades one, where model to model conversations settle. What is thin is work that follows a value through the loop itself, across settings and seeds.

caption: One round of the loop, read as one generation
narration: One round is one generation. For each prompt the organism writes six candidate answers. That is the population. The judge compares each against an alternative and keeps the two it prefers. That is selection. Training runs on those two. That is inheritance. Held-out prompts measure the value again.

caption: The two organisms, and how the trait under selection is scored
narration: Every population needs a measured trait. I fine-tuned Qwen three four B and OLMo three seven B with value orientations. The gambling organism's value is the share of answers picking the risky gamble. The insecure-code organism's is how insecure its answers to three fixed questions about its coding habits read, scored zero to one by its frozen base model.

headline: The selection differential: kept answers minus the whole pool
sub: the mean value of the two kept answers minus the mean over all six candidates
narration: The first term carries over untouched. The selection differential here is the mean value score of the two kept answers minus the mean over all six candidates in that prompt's pool. I call it the selector gap.

headline: Here the response coefficient is one, with nothing fitted
sub: the next measured value is just the mean of the kept answers
narration: The second term is where the analogy stops being decorative. In breeding, heritability has to be fitted. Here it comes out at one, with nothing fitted, so the next measured value is just the kept candidates' mean.

caption: Next value equals the kept candidate mean, held out by condition
narration: Holding out one complete experimental condition at a time, across three hundred forty rounds, that rule misses the next measured value by zero point zero eight one. Assuming no change misses by zero point one two eight. The value is re-read on held-out prompts, not on the answers trained on.

caption: Spread and agreement, with the recipe for each
narration: Breeders do better than waiting: they forecast the differential from the variation available and the strength of selection. Spread is the standard deviation of a prompt's candidate value scores, averaged over the round's prompts. Agreement is the correlation between the judge's scores and those value scores.

caption: Agreement times spread, and the same step iterated
narration: Their product forecasts the gap before the judge runs. Across three hundred sixty-seven rounds with logged judge scores, agreement times spread reconstructs the realized gaps at an error of zero point zero four zero. On matched rounds it predicts the next value at zero point one zero zero, against zero point zero eight five using the kept mean itself.

caption: Generations iterated forward from first-round measurements
narration: Breeders iterate generations, so I did too. Spread, agreement, and pool composition come from round one, stay fixed, and the update repeats. Endpoints land at zero point one one eight, against zero point four three one for no change. On the thirty-two self-only four-round runs here, zero point one five nine.

caption: Drift and finite sampling, entered stage by stage
narration: Real breeding programs do not follow the equation exactly. Finite populations drift, and traits are read off samples. Here the value comes from a limited number of sampled answers, the judge's picks land near the forecast gap, training lands near the kept mean, and agreement wanders. Each stage gets a noise term sized from the residuals.

caption: Simulated draws against the observed trajectories, run by run
narration: Sampled forward, it reproduces the shape of the real trajectories. Total round-to-round movement, zero point seven zero nine against zero point six four eight observed. Direction changes per run, one point two two against one point two zero. Eighty-nine percent of observed endpoints fall inside the eighty percent band.

headline: The judge is not a fixed environment sitting outside the population
sub: two model families · small models · short runs · filtered supervised fine-tuning · two narrow behaviors
narration: A breeder's criterion sits outside the population. This one does not. Agreement depends on the candidate distribution in front of the judge, and training keeps changing that distribution, so agreement drifts during a run. Most of the remaining error lives there. The scope is narrow: two model families, small models, short runs, filtered supervised fine-tuning, two behaviors.

caption: Reaching into a running loop through spread and agreement
narration: Breeders do not only describe selection, they run it. Mixing base-model answers into a pool whose candidates had collapsed to identical scores restored spread, and a stuck value eroded. Swapping in a min-risk oracle judge, setting agreement to minus one, reversed a run near the top of the scale.

kicker: SELECTION MECHANISMS ARE THINGS YOU CAN ENGINEER
checks: spread — how much the round's candidates differ
agreement — which way the judge sorts that variation
what the training step does with the kept answers
closer: Natural and cultural selection sculpted human values; artificial selection is something we get to design.
narration: A century of breeding taught that a selection mechanism is something you build. As A I takes over more of its own post-training, someone chooses what variation those loops offer and which way they sort it. Natural and cultural selection sculpted human values. Artificial selection is something we get to design.
